chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Earl Hines and the influences that make a style
summary: Freeman credits Earl Hines with introducing the Harlem pianists, and describes his own style as a ball of many influences.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, listen, we've got you out of Chicago. So, all right, --

I wanted to add and I think it is only fair to add, if I did not say this, that Jess was not only influenced by Louis and Bix, but certainly by Earl Hines, as I think we all were. Earl Hines had a style of playing -- now, here, it was Earl Hines who told me about the James P. Johnsons, the Fats Wallers, the Lucky Roberts and the Lion, because he knew, he was from Pittsburgh. He was in the east. He came out to Chicago
Yes, I think it should be said, too.
Of course, it's great to see Earl -- Earl has become an idol now and he's busier than ever he would want to be.
Yes. It's there to hear. You can definitely hear that -- it isn't anything that he's -- anything that he has physically picked up from Earl but it's in that rolling style --

No one had played like that before or since, and of course, Jess became his own man after many years of listening -- there's a little thing I say about myself when people ask me if any saxophone player influenced me, I say with all due respect to the great Coleman Hawkins, I was influenced by so many different things, the black dancers, the black singers, the pianist, the clarinet players, the drummers, that I like to feel that all of this and here I go with the again mania has rolled itself up into a -- sort of a Freemanistic ball in music. Does that make any sense?
Yes, and that is what I think happened to Jess. I think his playing became his own.
Yes, and he always did like singers
Take all of the influences of Lester Young, yet look at how much his own man he became.
After all, that's the proper thing for evoluation, isn't it?
Yes, of course. We are all influenced by somebody and we always will be and we need to be influenced if we are going to be working.
And it's like growth, it's how you develop--
I think Eddie Condon said a very funny thing once, 'Can you imagine music that doesn't sound like music?'
